description: Local Environmental Observer (LEO) Network is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium; EPA Pacific Northwest Region; DHHS Indian Health Service, Alaska Area. This site encourages members to post unique or unusual environmental events onto public, web-based maps. The network provides a model for connecting community members with technical experts and resources. To contribute to the site, users must join LEO and set up a personal profile. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Drought, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
